decision: Standing user choice for this run: every rule that clears the precision gate enters the queue, nothing is deferred. All three rules scored pattern_precision 1.0 with status PASS and queue_eligible true in 01.5-precision-report.json (CORBA_REMOVAL 60/60 judged out of a 333-hit population, TLS_ANON_CIPHER_DISABLED 2/2 census, CLDR_LOCALE_DATA_DEFAULT 5/5 census). CORBA_REMOVAL (HIGH) and TLS_ANON_CIPHER_DISABLED (MEDIUM) are mandatory breaking changes; CLDR_LOCALE_DATA_DEFAULT (LOW) is queued rather than deferred under the same standing choice. The on-disk order here is by severity; the binding execution order is computed by effective_rule_order, which ranks body-local ahead of signature, so the two body-local rules run before CORBA_REMOVAL. REVISION: TLS_ANON_CIPHER_DISABLED was removed from the queue and deferred. Its only mechanical fix strips the 'anon' token from jdk.tls.disabledAlgorithms at runtime, re-enabling unauthenticated cipher suites. That is a security policy decision for the maintainers, not a migration transform, so the shard was reverted to baseline and the rule deferred. See 05-deferred-TLS_ANON_CIPHER_DISABLED.json. REVISION 2: CLDR_LOCALE_DATA_DEFAULT was also removed and deferred. Its fix hard-codes the JDK 8 COMPAT date pattern, which keeps output byte-identical across locale providers but drops locale sensitivity in the GUI tools. The recipe itself recorded NEEDS_REVIEW on all five sites; raising that to FIXED to satisfy the gate would be exactly the fabricated status the pipeline forbids. Work preserved on tag wip/tls-cldr-changes.

ordering_reasons.reason: binding dependency order — dependent transforms first
